instruction: Look at straight_slot_block.step in SOLIDWORKS with the SOLIDWORKS CAM add-in. On this machine, start SOLIDWORKS 2025 from the desktop shortcut and use its installed SOLIDWORKS CAM/CAMWorks add-in; there is no separate SolidCAM desktop program in this image. Create a 3-axis Milling CAM-Part for straight_slot_block.step from a single top-side setup. Use standard SOLIDWORKS CAM Slot, Profile, or Contour operations to machine the four visible straight slots/keyways on the top face. Each slot must be machined along its full modeled length down to the modeled slot floor; one operation per slot or an equivalent grouped slot operation is acceptable as long as all four slots are included in the posted NC program. Use only 3-axis milling for this task; do not use rotary, indexed, or simultaneous 5-axis machining. Use suitable installed flat end mill or slotting tool-library entries; exact tool station numbers, spindle speeds, feedrates, and internal tool-library IDs may follow stable SOLIDWORKS CAM Technology Database defaults. Keep SOLIDWORKS CAM's default generated NC comments; do not rename operations just to add labels. Save the required output file(s) to the Desktop: C:\Users\User\Desktop\task-19.nc. Generate the required NC/G-code file(s) by using SOLIDWORKS CAM's normal Post Process workflow after calculating the toolpath, with an installed .ctl postprocessor from C:\ProgramData\SOLIDWORKS\SOLIDWORKS CAM 2025\Posts. For this milling task, prefer m3axis-tutorial.ctl, mach_iii.ctl, or haas_vf3.ctl. If the generated program opens in NC Editor or is initially saved with a different extension, use Save As from that generated program to save the exact requested Desktop filename(s).
source: SOLIDWORKS CAM 2025 official documentation: https://help.solidworks.com/2025/english/WhatsNew/c_wn_cam.htm ; SOLIDWORKS CAM 2025 Contour Mill toolpaths: https://help.solidworks.com/2025/English/WhatsNew/c_wn2025_cam_contour_mill_toolpaths.htm
